impact_surface_review: LOG-002 impact surface is mostly sufficient for a small reversible build: js/core/LevelManager.js for derived read-only wave progress, main.js for transition/HUD/audio/stat ownership, index.html/css/game.css for DOM HUD and non-blocking toast.

config/levels.json should remain excluded. The requested HUD/progress work does not require tuning or data migration, and current LevelManager already owns totalOnions/maxAliveOnions/spawnIntervalMs/spawnedOnions.

Player/Bullet/Onion/OnionAI must remain forbidden. resetGame(nextLevel,false) intentionally rebuilds those objects through existing loadLevel(); changing entity behavior would turn this into a physical-continuity rewrite outside this task.

js/ui/canvas.js should remain conditionally allowed only for narrow responsive sizing math if CSS/index.html cannot prevent overlap. It is already the global canvas sizing owner and currently sizes from viewport/padding without reserving sibling panel width, so excluding it outright would create a known desktop overflow risk for a persistent side panel. It must not receive gameplay logic, HUD content, wave math, stats, or input behavior.
Removing the unused drawHUD() from main.js is acceptable only after build re-runs rg and confirms no call site; this is cleanup inside the approved HUD ownership change, not a canvas-HUD redesign.
call_site_review: Wave completion call site is main.js update(): levelManager.isWaveComplete() then resetGame(nextLevel,false), playLevelupSfx(), fadeBgm(0,800), engine.stop(), showLevelOverlay(nextLevel), input.endFrame(), return. Replacing only fadeBgm(0,800), engine.stop(), and showLevelOverlay(nextLevel) matches the requested behavior and leaves completion rule intact.

resetGame(level, resetState) calls levelManager.loadLevel(), refreshes player/onions, sets bullet bounces, and resets state only when resetState is true. It does not update stats.maxLevel or HUD. Build must add an explicit maxLevel/localStorage update after the continuous transition because startEngineIfReady() returns early while engine.running is true.

showLevelOverlay() has no direct call site except the current wave-completion branch. Keeping the function and #level-overlay markup is safe; the build must ensure no wave-completion path calls it after the patch.

hideLevelOverlay() is still used by showGameOver(), jumpToLevel(), and resetGame-adjacent flows. It also stops level-up SFX. Do not remove it; add an independent toast/audio cleanup path for continuous level-up.

isOverlayActive() is used by title float suppression, game time/playMs accounting, players panel visibility, lifecycle resume/focus, pause key handling, and exported debug/runtime helpers. The new toast/HUD must not add a visible class checked by isOverlayActive() and must use pointer-events:none or equivalent so input remains live.

Audio surface is in main.js through wrappers and js/ui/audio.js already exposes fadeLevelupSfx(). Build should use existing main.js fadeLevelupSfx(durationMs) wrapper or add a timer in main.js, not edit sounds/assets or audio controller unless a proven wrapper gap appears.

drawSpeedDot call sites are inside mutually exclusive draw() branches: arena clipped branch and fallback no-arena branch. No Speed Dot rendering fix is approved unless build proves a real duplicate after current dirty-worktree contents are considered.

HUD: drawHUD() is a stale canvas HUD definition with no call site. DOM HUD ownership in main.js/index.html/css/game.css is safer than reviving drawHUD(). Existing #players-panel is online-gated by onlineService.hasPlayersPanel and should not be reused for permanent run HUD.
regression_risks: Continuous reset uses resetGame(nextLevel,false), which preserves score/time/counters but recenters player, clears bullets, rebuilds arena/onions and resets Speed Dot through LevelManager.loadLevel(). This tradeoff is acceptable for v1 only because physical continuity is explicitly out of scope; review must call it out to the tester.

maxLevel/stat reporting can regress silently: onlineService.writeStats() sends stats.maxLevel each update, but stats.maxLevel only updates in startEngineIfReady() and showGameOver(). Continuous wave transitions need immediate maxLevel/localStorage update in main.js.

Level-up SFX can linger because hideLevelOverlay() currently stops it. New non-blocking feedback needs its own timeout/fade using fadeLevelupSfx(), and should cancel/replace an older toast timer if transitions happen quickly.
BGM should not fade to zero on normal wave completion. Chase/pause/gameover/jumpToLevel/play-again/continue BGM behavior must remain unchanged.

DOM HUD can create layout overflow. #layout is flex with a viewport-sized canvas; js/ui/canvas.js currently computes canvas size from viewport padding and not sibling widths. CSS should be attempted first; if overlap remains, a small canvas sizing change is justified.

Progress math must be derived, read-only, and aligned with completion: activePressureCount should include alive or dying onions via getPressureOnionCount(); completion remains budget exhausted plus zero pressure. HUD text must not drive progression.

Potential stale overlay assumptions: removing showLevelOverlay from wave completion means its timeout no longer restarts the engine. The new branch must leave engine running and return cleanly after input.endFrame(); no startEngineIfReady() call is needed for that branch unless engine was explicitly stopped, which it should not be.
